problems: The door's rectangular lower part and its round top piece have their front faces in exactly the same plane, so the surfaces flicker against each other: a dark half-disc shadow covers the upper door and a torn notch shows at the arch line. The restyle would keep it as a crack or stain. Make the round top piece slightly thinner so its lower half hides behind the rectangle, and give the rectangle a smaller rounded edge so only a clean joint line shows.

No night sky shows. The camera frames only the door leaf, so the stone wall fills the whole card and its coping (z 1.42-1.49) sits above the top edge. The brief's royal-blue sky with stars and moon has nowhere to appear, and the keystone of the arch is cut off at the top.

The stone arch surround is the door's own frame, but it is set as background, so it doesn't count for framing. That crops the card too tightly on the leaf, with the arch stones running off the top and the porch step cut at the bottom.
There is a visible horizontal seam across the door where the straight lower part meets the half-round top, because the round top is set slightly behind the front of the straight part.
